title: Competition-dominated microbial interactions and adaptive mutations enhance synthetic denitrifying community functions.
authors: Zhao, Zhenrui; Hu, Ruiwen; Zhou, Min; Guan, Xiaotong; Huang, Huaxia; Ding, Lang; Qian, Lu; Ming, Yuzhen; Niu, Mingyang; Wu, Kun; Yu, Xiaoli; Yan, Qingyun; Shu, Longfei; He, Qiang; He, Zhili
one_liner_zh: 该文研究合成反硝化群落中种间竞争与适应性突变对群落功能的影响，虽使用AlphaFold2和分子对接辅助分析突变效应，但核心是生态学实验而非蛋白质结构计算建模，方法贡献较弱。
abstract: Understanding how interspecific interactions shape ecosystem functioning is a fundamental and longstanding question in ecology, especially along an evolutionary trajectory. Here, we used experimental evolution to evaluate how microbial interactions and adaptive mutations shaped community-level functions in synthetic denitrifying communities (SDCs) along a species richness gradient (one, two, and six species). Our results showed that competitive microbial interactions were observed and significantly (P < 0.05) enhanced denitrification rates in the six-species SDCs during experimental evolution. Genome and metagenome re-sequencing analysis revealed the highest fixed non-synonymous and frameshift mutations within the six-species SDCs, among genes involved in nutrient transport, DNA repair, and secretion pathways. AlphaFold2 protein structure prediction, molecular docking, and Evo 2 host fitness prediction indicated that the fixed mutations could improve host strain fitness, and partial least squares path modeling (PLS-PM) further revealed that interspecific competition accelerated adaptive mutations, thereby reinforcing community-level functions, indicating potential Red Queen dynamics. This study offers novel insights into our understanding of eco-evolutionary mechanisms linking species richness, microbial interactions, adaptive mutations, and community functions, with important implications for active nitrogen removal and greenhouse gas mitigation in diverse ecosystems. IMPORTANCE: Microbial diversity is widely recognized as a key driver of ecosystem functioning, yet how species interactions shape ecosystem functions through evolutionary processes remains poorly understood. Using synthetic denitrifying communities with different levels of species richness, we show that interspecific competition can accelerate adaptive mutations and enhance community-level denitrification over evolutionary timescales. Communities with higher species richness accumulated more adaptive mutations, particularly in genes associated with nutrient transport, DNA repair, and secretion systems, ultimately improving microbial fitness and denitrification performance. Our findings provide direct experimental evidence that microbial competition can promote functional adaptation, consistent with the Red Queen hypothesis. This study advances our understanding of the eco-evolutionary mechanisms linking species richness, microbial interactions, adaptive evolution, and ecosystem functioning.
abstract_zh: 理解种间互作如何塑造生态系统功能是生态学中一个基础且长期存在的问题，尤其是在进化轨迹背景下。在此，我们利用实验进化评估了微生物互作和适应性突变如何沿物种丰富度梯度（一、二和六个物种）在合成反硝化群落（SDCs）中塑造群落水平功能。结果表明，在实验进化过程中，六物种SDCs中观察到竞争性微生物互作，并显著（P < 0.05）增强了反硝化速率。基因组和宏基因组重测序分析显示，六物种SDCs中涉及营养转运、DNA修复和分泌途径的基因中固定了最高的非同义和移码突变。AlphaFold2蛋白质结构预测、分子对接和Evo 2宿主适应性预测表明，固定突变可提高宿主菌株适应性，偏最小二乘路径建模（PLS-PM）进一步揭示，种间竞争加速了适应性突变，从而增强了群落水平功能，表明存在潜在的Red Queen动力学。本研究为理解连接物种丰富度、微生物互作、适应性突变和群落功能的生态进化机制提供了新见解，对多样化生态系统中的活性氮去除和温室气体减排具有重要意义。重要性：微生物多样性被广泛认为是生态系统功能的关键驱动因素，但物种互作如何通过进化过程塑造生态系统功能仍知之甚少。利用不同物种丰富度水平的合成反硝化群落，我们表明种间竞争可在进化时间尺度上加速适应性突变并增强群落水平反硝化作用。物种丰富度较高的群落积累了更多适应性突变，特别是在与营养转运、DNA修复和分泌系统相关的基因中，最终提高了微生物适应性和反硝化性能。我们的发现提供了直接实验证据，表明微生物竞争可促进功能适应，这与Red Queen假说一致。本研究推进了我们对连接物种丰富度、微生物互作、适应性进化和生态系统功能的生态进化机制的理解。
